status: Separately specified diagnostic after observing the individual and team primary results; not untouched confirmation. The six main protocols and source remain frozen. No audit outcome tunes those runs.
question: How much controllable tactic headroom is present, and do direction switches actually require different best tactics?
procedure: Enumerate both legal actions for each isolated role, or all eight squad combinations, for every reserved world/player seed and both directions used by each main study. One actual fight per forced action is sufficient to enumerate these deterministic conditional worlds; bot randomness is counter-based and resets per encounter. Preserve complete real-core fixed-choice traces and actual combat. Do not use table results in online policies.
metrics: Fraction of direction pairs with disjoint best-action sets (requiring a different optimal choice), treating ties as sets
Fraction of pairs whose best-action sets change but still overlap
Fraction of observed feedback eligible for training
Offline best-action damage minus the main primary comparator: an optimistic upper bound, not a learned policy
verification: Independent policy feedback replay, full combat replay, and equality between each fresh main-study fight and its corresponding forced-action table entry for damage, health, duration, enemy outcomes and input fingerprint.
limits: Post-hoc diagnostic on examined generators, with new counterfactual measurements.
Optimal means best among this small authored tactic set for a particular fixed world/controller parameter realization.
The table is an offline oracle and must not be presented as learned foresight.
A direction reversal need not change the optimal tactic. Warm-start benefit or lack of baiting harm alone cannot establish strategy-specific recall or adversarial robustness.
Do not discard insensitive cases or alter success thresholds after seeing the audit. Use findings to design a separately specified next benchmark.
